lines.text: You tap your phone hundreds of times a day. Your finger never actually touches the screen.
Under the glass is a grid of transparent electrodes, etched into the surface and invisible to you.
Each one forms a tiny capacitor. The glass between it and your finger is an insulator, so no current crosses.
Your finger is conductive. It bends the electric field through the glass, and the controller reads the change at every node.
If you land between two nodes, it compares their readings and works out where you touched. The coordinate can fall anywhere.
That is why gloves fail. Insulate the field and the grid sees nothing at all.
The whole interface runs on an electric field you cannot feel. You were never touching anything.
